title: Making water
summary: Hydrogen gas burns in oxygen to make water, releasing a lot of energy.

reactants.title: Reactants
reactants.caption: Two hydrogen molecules (H₂) and one oxygen molecule (O₂). In each molecule the atoms are held together by a covalent bond, where they share electrons.

approach.title: Molecules approach
approach.caption: The molecules move toward each other. For a reaction to happen they must collide with enough energy and in the right way.

break.title: Bonds break
break.caption: Breaking the H–H and O=O bonds takes in energy. This starting energy is the activation energy; in real life a spark or flame supplies it.

rearrange.title: Atoms rearrange
rearrange.caption: The free atoms move and regroup. Atoms are never created or destroyed, so all 4 hydrogen atoms and both oxygen atoms end up in the products.

form.title: New bonds form
form.caption: New O–H bonds form, making two water molecules. Forming bonds releases energy as heat and light, so the reaction is exothermic.

products.title: Products
products.caption: Two molecules of water (H₂O). More energy was released making four O–H bonds than was needed to break the old bonds, so the surroundings get hotter.

notes.mechanism: Simplified model. Real hydrogen–oxygen combustion is a chain reaction with short-lived pieces such as H•, O• and OH•, and bonds break and form at overlapping times. The animation shows the overall idea: bonds break, atoms rearrange, new bonds form.
notes.thermo: ΔH = −483.6 kJ for 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O when the water is steam (−571.6 kJ if it condenses to liquid). The bond-energy sum below uses average values, so it is close to, not exactly, the measured value.
